From:             Dennis Galvin
To:               "Alan Blind"
Cc:               Petition Resource
Subject:          NRC Staff’s 2.206 Initial Assessment of Palisades Restart 2.206 Petitions and Supplemental Information
                  Submitted from May 15, 2025, to April 2, 2026
Date:             Friday, October 9, 2026 12:22:00 PM
Attachments:      OEDO-25-00290 2.206 Petition - Palisades Restart - Mr. Alan Blind - 2026-10-09 Initial Assessment.pdf


Dear Mr. Blind,

The purpose of this email is to convey the results of the petition review board (PRB) initial
assessment in accordance with NRC Management Directive (MD) 8.11, “Review Process
for 10 CFR 2.206 Petitions” and its associated Directive Handbook (DH) Section III.E
“Informing the Petitioner of the Results of the Initial PRB Assessment” (Agencywide
Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML18296A043) for
the Palisades Restart 2.206 petitions from May 15, 2025, to April 2, 2026.

Initial Assessment Results

The PRB’s initial assessment is that the petition does not meet the acceptance criteria in
either MD 8.11 DH Section III.C.1(a) or MD 8.11 DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii).

       The facts specified in the petition do not provide support for the requested action, MD
       8.11 DH Section III.C.1(a).
       The issues raised have previously been the subject of a facility-specific or generic
       NRC staff review, MD 8.11 DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii).
       The petition does not provide significant new information that the staff did not
       consider in the prior review, MD 8.11 DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii).

Based on these acceptance criteria not being met, our initial assessment is to not accept
your petition for review. The details of the initial assessment are attached.

Opportunity for Public Meeting

Following your review of this PRB initial assessment, I would be happy to offer you the
opportunity to clarify your petition in a virtual public meeting with the PRB. If you decide to
take advantage of this opportunity, the meeting with the PRB would be conducted
consistent with the format described in MD 8.11, DH Section III.F. The PRB will consider
your statements and information presented at the meeting, along with the original petition,
as supplemented, in making its final determination on whether to accept your petition for
review. Please indicate by October 16, 2026, whether you wish to have this public meeting
before we close the petition.

If you have any questions regarding this e-mail, please feel free to contact me at
Dennis.Galvin@nrc.gov.

Respectfully,

Dennis Galvin
Project Manager / Agency 2.206 Petition Coordinator
 U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation
Division of Licensing Projects 1
Operating Licensing Branch 2
301-415-6256
          10 CFR 2.206 PETITION REGARDING THE PALISADES NUCLEAR PLANT

                      PETITION REVIEW BOARD INITIAL ASSESSMENT

                          OEDO-25-00290, EPID L-2025-CRS-0000

Petition Submittals

By emails dated between May 15, 2025, and April 2, 2026 (see details below), you made a total
of 14 submissions of petitions to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) for consideration
under Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR), Section 2.206. The submissions
requested various enforcement actions against Holtec Decommissioning International, LLC, and
Holtec Palisades, LLC (collectively Holtec) regarding the Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP or
Palisades). As documented in my acknowledgment emails dated December 1, 2025, and
December 15, 2025, you withdrew 7 of the 14 submissions. The open and withdrawn
submissions are listed below and grouped by topic. The withdrawn petitions are not further
discussed.

Withdrawn Submittals

May 15, 2025 **       ML25136A365      Submission of Steam Generator (SG) Condition
June 21, 2025 **      ML25183A334      Monitoring and Operational Assessments
July 22, 2025 **      ML25204A144
August 8, 2025 **     ML25223A096

                                       Related Fire Protection Modifications*

The specific requests and the associated concerns will be identified and discussed within each
topic.

2.206 Process and Initial Assessment Results

On September 30, 2025 (ML25329A215), I informed you that the NRC staff had screened the
then 13 submissions into the 2.206 process in accordance with NRC Management Directive
(MD) 8.11, “Review Process for 10 CFR 2.206 Petitions,” and its associated Directive Handbook
(DH) Section II.A.2(d) (ML18296A043). I also informed you that the NRC staff concluded,
following review in accordance with MD 8.11, DH Section II.B.1, that the concerns expressed in
your submissions did not warrant immediate enforcement action. A Petition Review Board
(PRB) has evaluated whether to accept the submissions for review in accordance with MD 8.11,
DH Section III.C, “Criteria for Petition Evaluation,” and has performed an initial assessment of
the submissions in accordance with MD 8.11, DH Section III.D, “PRB Initial Assessment.”

The PRB’s initial assessment is that the submissions do not meet the acceptance criteria in
either MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(a) or MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii). MD 8.11, DH Section
III.C.1(a) is not met if the facts specified in the petition do not provide support for the requested
action. MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii) is not met if the “issues raised have previously been
the subject of a facility-specific or generic NRC staff review…” and the petition does not provide
significant new information that the staff did not consider in the prior review. Based on either of
these acceptance criteria not being met, our initial assessment is to not accept your
submissions for review.

The NRC staff notes that the submissions make many requests for specific activities by the
NRC staff, such as conducting inspections, conducting reviews, holding meetings, or preparing
reports. The regulations in 10 CFR 2.206(a) provide that any person may file a request to
institute a proceeding pursuant to 10 CFR 2.202 to modify, suspend, or revoke a license, or for
any other action as may be proper, on a licensee or other person subject to the jurisdiction of
the Commission. The regulations in 10 CFR 2.206(a) do not provide for requesting specific
activities by the NRC staff and thus any requests for such activities are outside the scope of the
2.206 process and thus are not applicable. The discussion below will distinguish between
requests in scope and out of scope of the 2.206 process.

1. Inspection of a Previously Replaced Containment Tendon

Your June 3, 2025 (ML25157A006), submittal, as supplemented by your July 22, 2025
(ML25204A143), submittal involves a containment tendon replaced as part of the Palisades SG
replacement project completed in 1991. Your submissions designated the containment tendon
as 388F or 38BF. The license letter dated August 26, 1991 (ML18057B250), designated the
containment tendon as 38BF, so the NRC will use designation for the remainder of the
discussion. Your submissions requested the NRC to perform the following:

   1. Recognize that the omission of tendon 38BF from Holtec’s [containment structural
      integrity] surveillance program constitutes a failure to comply with approved Technical
      Specifications (TSs) 5.5.5, and 5.6.7, and surveillance requirement (SR) 3.6.1.2;




                                                  2
    2. Require Holtec to perform inspection and analysis of tendon 38BF prior to NRC
      acceptance of the 2025 tendon surveillance report or authorization of Palisades’ entry
      into Mode 4.

You provided the following concerns as the basis and justification for the requested enforcement
actions:

   1. Tendon 38BF, the sole containment tendon that was replaced during the Palisades
      1990-1991 SG replacement project, is unique and subject to early prestress relaxation.
      Therefore, Tendon 38BF is not representative of other Palisades containment tendons.
      Therefore, Tendon 38BF should be excluded from random sampling but should be
      inspected because of its uniqueness.

   2. Because Tendon 38BF was not inspected, the licensee failed to comply with TSs 5.5.5,
      and 5.6.7, and SR 3.6.1.2;

The following history shows that the NRC considered the need for inspection of Tendon 38BF
following the Palisades SG replacement project, but the NRC accepted the licensee proposal
not to include Tendon 38BF in the containment structural integrity surveillance program.

By letter dated February 12, 1991 (ML18057A752), the licensee informed the NRC that the
restoration of the temporary opening in the Palisades containment to support the SG
replacement project had been completed. The licensee also informed the NRC that one tendon,
Tendon 38BF, was damaged while creating the opening and was replaced with a new, identical
cable.

In NRC Inspection Report 50-255/90025, dated May 24, 1991 (ML18057A939), Section 6.c,
“Tendon· Surveillance Requirements for the Replaced Tendon (37700),” the NRC staff stated in
part,

       It is the NRC's position that the replaced tendon should be. included in the 1992
       scheduled surveillance. This is based on the NRC technical staff and Bechtel
       experience which indicates that the majority of a new tendon's detensioning
       occurs during the first year or two. Therefore, an inspection in 1992 would show if
       the replaced tendon had detensioned. The NRC staff is not requiring that the
       ongoing surveillance program be adjusted for a single tendon, but does consider
       inclusion of this tendon in the 1992 surveillance to be prudent. Inclusion of this
       tendon into the 1992 planned surveillance is considered an Open Item
       (255/90025-06).

By letter dated August 16, 1991 (ML18057B250), the licensee stated that it will not include
Tendon 38BF in the tendon surveillance program. The licensee justified its position by indicating
that (1) the tendon has significant accessibility issues, and (2) as a unique tendon it would
provide limited information on the condition of the Palisades containment building compared to a
randomly selected tendon.

In NRC Inspection Report 50-255/90025, dated April 14, 1992 (ML18058A354), Section 2.d,
“(Closed) Open Item 255/90025-06,” the NRC accepted the licensee's surveillance program for
the replaced containment tendon and closed the open item. Therefore, Tendon 38BF does not
need to be included in the licensee’s containment structural integrity surveillance program and
its omission did not constitute a failure to comply with TSs 5.5.5, and 5.6.7, and SR 3.6.1.2.


                                               3
 Based on the foregoing, the acceptance criteria in MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(b)(ii) are not met
since the “issues raised have previously been the subject of a facility-specific or generic NRC
staff review…” and the petition does not provide significant new information that the staff did not
consider in the prior review. Based on this acceptance criteria not being met, our initial
assessment is to not accept these submissions for review.

2. Notification of Readiness for Transition to Power Operations Licensing Basis

Your July 28, 2025, submittal (ML25209A504), requested the NRC to perform the following:

Before Fuel Receipt and Loading:

   1. Require Holtec to resubmit the July 1, 2025, Notification of Readiness for
      Transition to Power Operations Licensing Basis letter (ML25182A066) under
      oath or affirmation, consistent with NRC regulations and guidance;

   2. Suspend the effectiveness of the license amendments and exemption issued on
      July 24, 2025 (as described in NRC Commission Staff Notification
      ML25205A193), until such time as the July 1, 2025, letter is properly submitted
      under oath or affirmation;

   3. Evaluate whether the absence of an oath or affirmation undermines the validity of
      NRC Staff's reliance on the July 1, 2025, letter in conditioning the effective date
      of fuel receipt, fuel loading, and operational authorization;

Before Palisades Restart Panel Consideration or Approving Reactor Operation

   4. Complete a supplemental inspection under NRC Inspection Procedure,
      Evaluations of Changes, Tests, and Experiments, to independently assess
      Holtec’s implementation of 10 CFR 50.59 at Palisades and ensure licensing
      basis changes are being properly evaluated and controlled and to provide
      assurance the extent of condition from the violations at the Camden Corporate
      office do not extend to the Palisades restart;

   5. Complete a Design Bases Assurance Inspection under NRC Inspection
      Procedure to verify that key systems, structures, and components required for
      safe operation are being maintained in conformance with the plant’s current
      licensing basis prior to restart to provide assurance the extent of condition from
      the violations at the Camden Corporate office do not extend to the Palisades
      restart.

Note that Items 4 and 5 request the NRC to perform certain activities unrelated to the
enforcement process. As noted above, the regulations in 10 CFR 2.206(a) do not provide for
requesting specific activities by the NRC staff and thus these requests are outside the scope of
the 2.206 process and are not applicable.

The letter that is the subject of this petition was submitted by the licensee on July 1, 2025,
“Notification of Readiness for Transition to Power Operations Licensing Basis” (ML25182A066).
The stated purpose of the letter was to report the licensing and regulatory activities needed to
support the resumption of power operations at Palisades and the licensee’s readiness to


                                                 4
 implement the power operations licensing basis (i.e., transition from decommissioning status to
operating status). The proposed implementation date for Palisades transition was August 25,
2025. The information in the letter was used by the NRC staff to inform the required
implementation date for the amendment and was not relied on to prepare the amendment safety
evaluation.

The basis for the petition relies on misquotes of 10 CFR 50.30(b), “Oath and affirmation” and
Regulatory Issue Summary (RIS) 2001-18, “Requirements for Oath or Affirmation,” dated
August 22, 2001 (ML010990211). The petition asserts that oath and affirmation are required for
licensee submittals that trigger some undefined NRC licensing authority rather than documents
relied upon to prepare safety evaluations for licenses or license amendments, as described
below.

The applicable regulation for oath or affirmation for nuclear power reactors is in 10 CFR
50.30(b), “Oath or affirmation.”

       Each application for a standard design approval or license, including, whenever
       appropriate, a construction permit or early site permit, or amendment of it, and
       each amendment of each application must be executed in a signed original by
       the applicant or duly authorized officer thereof under oath or affirmation.

The petition inappropriately designates 10 CFR 50.30(b) as 10 CFR 50.30(b)(1), and points to a
10 CFR 50.30(b)(2) which does not exist.

The petition misquotes RIS 2001-18 as follows:

       "Documents submitted to the NRC which are docketed and used to support
       licensing actions must be submitted under oath or affirmation. This includes
       requests for licensing actions and responses to requests for additional
       information that will be used in preparation of a safety evaluation."

RIS 2001-18 does not mention “support licensing actions” and directly ties oath and affirmation
to documents that will be used by the NRC staff to prepare a safety evaluation. Under the
heading, “Background Information,” RIS 2001-18 states in part:

       An oath or affirmation or its alternative, as described in this RIS, is required for
       any docketed submittal related to a license application, license amendment,
       supplemental information, or response to a request for additional information
       (RAI) that will be used by the NRC staff to prepare a safety evaluation that
       approves or denies a license or license amendment.

Under the heading, “Summary of Issue,” RIS 2001-18 states in part:

       Docketed submittals related to applications, license amendments, supplemental
       information, and responses to RAIs that will be used by the NRC staff to prepare
       a safety evaluation and to approve or deny an amendment to a license must be
       provided under oath or affirmation or an unsworn declaration.

Since the licensee’s July 1, 2025, letter provided information used in the implementation part of
the amendment and did not provide information relied on to prepare the amendment safety
evaluation, the July 1, 2025, letter was appropriately not submitted under oath and affirmation.


                                                 5
 Since the licensee’s July 1, 2025, letter provided information used in the implementation part of
the amendment and did not provide information relied on to prepare the amendment safety
evaluation, the July 1, 2025, letter was appropriately not submitted under oath and affirmation.
Based on the foregoing, the acceptance criteria in MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(a) are not met
since the facts specified in the petition do not constitute a basis for the requested action. Based
on this acceptance criteria not being met, our initial assessment is to not accept this submission
for review.

3. Implementation of NTTF 2.1

Your August 6, 2025 (ML25218A228), submittal, as supplemented by your April 2, 2026
(ML26098A013) submittal, requested the following (the April 2, 2026, submittal endorsed the
actions in the August 6, 2025, submittal):

   1. Reject Holtec’s proposed schedule for deferred completion of post-Fukushima seismic
      reevaluation activities unless and until NRC Staff formally reviews and approves that
      schedule as compliant with the 10 CFR 50.54(f) process and the NEI April 9, 2013,
      guidance. “Proposed Path Forward for NTTF Recommendation 2.1: Seismic
      Reevaluations” (ML13106A331).

   2. Issue an order prohibiting Holtec from entering Mode 6 or loading fuel at the Palisades
      Nuclear Plant unless one of the following conditions is met:

       a. Holtec has completed all required seismic reevaluation actions under NTTF
          Recommendation 2.1, including:

           o   Completion of the full Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SPRA);
           o   Use of SPRA insights to determine and implement required plant modifications,
               procedural changes, or compensatory strategies;
           o   Completion of Expedited Seismic Evaluation Process (ESEP) walkdowns and
               associated High Confidence of Low Probability of Failure (HCLPF) evaluations
               for inaccessible components;
           o   Submission of a final seismic reevaluation response to NRC addressing
               Enclosure 1 of the March 12, 2012 [ML12056A046], 50.54(f) letter.

   3. Or NRC Staff has formally reviewed and approved an alternative milestone schedule
      that includes justification based on Holtec’s submitting required information, for deferring
      these safety activities beyond fuel loading and startup.

   4. Require Holtec to revise its licensing basis or restart schedule to reflect timely
      compliance with these requirements, consistent with NRC expectations for sites
      classified as Category 4 under the NRC’s July 3, 2019, letter (ML19140A307) (i.e., sites
      whose reevaluated seismic hazards exceeded their design basis but were allowed to
      defer SPRA submittals solely because they were expected to permanently shut down
      prior to the SPRA due date) and the obligations set forth in the NEI April 9, 2013,
      implementation guidance.

Chronology of NTTF 2.1 Correspondence Applicable to the 2.206 Submissions

for some references (i.e. date or ADAMS No.) and ignore clearly applicable references (i.e. the

 licensee request and the NRC response for the SPRA deferral). In addition, given the volume of
correspondence applicable to the 2.206 submissions, and the different correspondence
applicable to each assertion, a chronology is presented for clarity.

Response to Petitioner Assertions

The basis for the request may be summarized by five assertions from the August 6, 2025, and
the April 2, 2026, submittals. The April 2, 2026, submittal refers to and repeats information from
the August 6, 2025, submittal, and thus the repeated information does not represent additional
assertions.

Assertion 1: Commitments were made pursuant to the NRC’s March 12, 2012, 50.54(f) letter,
and in accordance with NRC-endorsed NEI April 9, 2013, guidance. As such, they became
enforceable elements of the Palisades licensing basis. Holtec, as the successor licensee, is
bound by these commitments unless and until they are formally revised through an NRC-
approved process under 10 CFR § 50.90. [August 6, 2025, submission, Section I, Page 3]

NRC Response to Assertion 1

The assertion reflects a misunderstanding of the regulatory commitment process, essentially
asserts that regulatory commitment changes require NRC prior approval through the license
amendment process and ignores the explicit discussion of regulatory commitments in the NRC
May 8, 2019, response to the licensee’s March 20, 2019, request for deferral of actions related
to beyond-design-basis seismic hazard reevaluations. The NRC’s May 8, 2019, letter, under the
heading of “Regulatory Commitments,” discusses the management of regulatory commitments.

       In its deferral request letter dated March 20, 2019, the licensee proposed
       regulatory commitments to complete activities that will inform the SPRA. The
       NRC staff notes that NEI 99-04 "Guidelines for Managing NRC Commitments"
       (ADAMS Accession No. ML003680088), as endorsed by the NRC in SECY-00-
       0045, "Acceptance of NEI 99-04, "Guidelines for Managing NRC Commitments""
       (ADAMS Accession No. ML003679799), provides an acceptable method to
       manage commitments. If the licensee were to change these regulatory
       commitments, the staff expects to be informed in accordance with the process
       outlined in NEI 99-04, as endorsed by the NRC.

Unless commitments are incorporated explicitly into a facility licensing basis, such as being
made a license condition or incorporated into an updated final safety analysis report,
commitment changes may be made without prior NRC approval and do not require the submittal
of a license amendment request (LAR) (i.e., 10 CFR 50.90, referred to in the assertion, is the
regulation applicable to the submittal of LARs). Based on the assertion being factually wrong,
the acceptance criteria in MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(a) are not met since the facts specified in
the submission do not constitute a basis for the requested action. Based on this acceptance
criteria not being met, our initial assessment is to not accept this assertion for review.

Assertion 2: Holtec has neither fulfilled committed structural modifications to safety-related
Tanks T-53A, T-53B, and T-81, as described in the licensee’s December 18, 2014, letter nor


                                                8
 has requested and obtained NRC approval for deferral under 10 CFR § 50.90. [August 6, 2025,
submission, Section II, Page 5, with NRC clarifications] Further, the 2016 cancellation of the T-
81 modification was explicitly justified on the basis that SPRA insights would be used to
determine necessary safety improvements. [April 2, 2026, submission, Section IV, page 3]

NRC Response to Assertion 2

The assertion ignores Attachment 2, “Commitment Background (Historical) Information,” of the
licensee’s July 28, 2025, letter (i.e., the primary document associated with the assertion), which
addresses explicitly the committed modifications to Tanks T-53A, T-53B, and T-81. The licensee
letter specifically states that modifications to Tanks T-53A and T-53B were completed on
December 12, 2016, and the commitment associated with Tank T-81 was cancelled by licensee
letter dated April 18, 2016. The petitioner submission does not provide any justification that the
licensee’s stated completions of the Tanks T-53A and T-53B are inadequate, therefore, the
assertion regarding these tanks is without basis.

In its April 18, 2016, letter, the licensee made it clear that it did not base the cancellation of the
modification of Tank T-81 on the condition of using SPRA insights, as asserted by the petitioner,
but based the cancellation on an additional risk evaluation of Tank T-81 as discussed below.

The licensee discussed the subject tanks in its March 20, 2019, request for deferral of actions
related to beyond-design-basis seismic hazard reevaluations and the NRC May 8, 2019,
response. The licensee’s March 20, 2019, request, under the heading “Basis for SPRA
Deferral,” discusses that the licensee modified the anchorage of the two BASTs (i.e., Tanks
T-53A, T-53B). The licensee further discussed that while the ESEP determined that the PMST
(i.e., Tank T-81) required modification to enhance its seismic capability, subsequent reviews of
seismic risk have demonstrated that the tank is not risk significant and that modifications to
increase the seismic capacity of the tank are not warranted from a risk reduction perspective

The NRC reviewed the licensee discussion regarding tank modifications in its May 8, 2019,
letter, in Attachment 1 under the heading, “Consideration of Potential Cost-Justified Substantial
Safety Enhancements.” and found the licensee discussion in its March 20, 2019, letter
acceptable.

       In its deferral letter, the licensee reported to have completed the modifications to
       the BASTs. Also, in its deferral letter, the licensee mentioned that subsequent
       evaluations of seismic risk were completed to determine the seismic risk
       significance of the PMST. This subsequent evaluation was made available
       through an ePortal and the NRC staff reviewed it as part of the audit. Specifically,
       the licensee stated to have used the SPRA model to perform a sensitivity study
       by setting the fragility of the PMST to 0.0 g (always failed) instead of the baseline
       value of 0.48 g. After doing so, the licensee stated that the resulting CDF did not
       increase. For that reason, the licensee stated that the PMST is not risk significant
       from a seismic perspective, so enhancing its seismic capacity would not result in
       a substantial safety gain. After reviewing the supporting documents provided by
       the licensee, the staff did not identify any issues that would change the response
       to the deferral request.

As justification for the petition, you asserted that the licensee’s December 11, 2024, submittal,

(ML24346A171) did not comply with Commission Policy in SECY-12-0093, “Closure Options for
Generic Safety Issue - 191, Assessment of Debris Accumulation on Pressurized Water Reactor
Sump Performance,” dated July 9, 2012. By letter dated May 28, 2026, the licensee informed
the NRC that additional GL 2004-02 related testing and modifications would be performed and
provided an updated schedule. The discussion below is applicable to both the December 11,
2024, and May 28, 2026, schedule letters.

The PRB has determined that the facts presented in the petition involve multiple
misunderstandings of the status of GSI-191 resolution and the regulatory framework and do not
provide the basis for any enforcement action.

(a) GSI-191 is closed.

By memorandum dated July 23, 2019, the Director of the Office of Research closed GSI-191 in
response to the memorandum dated July 22, 2019 (ML19157A120) from the Director of the
NRC Office of Nuclear Regulation, which recommended the closure of GSI-191. As stated in the
December 11, 2024, Holtec letter, GL 2004-02, “Potential Impact of Debris Blockage on
Emergency Recirculation During Design Basis Accidents at Pressurized-Water Reactors,”
remains open for Palisades. The petition solely discusses GSI-191 and does not discuss
GL 2004-02.




                                                14
 (b) SECY-12-0093 is not Commission Policy

SECY or Commission papers are written issue papers the NRC staff submits to the Commission
to inform them about policy, rulemaking, and adjudicatory matters. SECY papers are not
Commission policy until acted upon by the Commission and only to the extent directed by the
Commission in a staff requirements memorandum (SRM). Thus, the actual Commission policy
is in SRM-SECY-12-0093, “Staff Requirements – SECY-12-0093 – Closure Options for Generic
Safety Issue - 191, Assessment of Debris Accumulation on Pressurized-Water Reactor Sump
Performance,” dated December 14, 2012 (ML12349A378), which makes several significant
clarifications to SECY-12-0093, including with regard to schedule. The petition does not discuss
SRM-SECY-12-0093.

(c) SRM-SECY-12-0093 supports reasonable plant specific implementation schedules.

The SRM discusses implementation schedules in part as follows:

       Given the vastly enlarged advanced strainers installed, compensatory measures
       already taken, and the low probability of challenging pipe breaks, adequate
       defense-in-depth is currently being maintained. The staff should be receptive to
       plant-specific implementation schedules that consider the cumulative effects of
       other required regulatory actions, licensee planned outages, critical
       modifications, maintenance activities, and occupational doses. The staff should
       remain open to staggering licensee submittals and the associated NRC reviews
       to accommodate the availability of staff and licensee resources.

The licensee has proposed actions ranging through the 4th quarter of 2027, in its May 28, 2026,
letter. The proposed schedule is consistent with above stated guidelines from SRM-SECY-
120093. As the petition does not discuss SRM-SECY-12-0093, it does not identify any
inconsistencies between the December 11, 2024, Holtec letter and SRM-SECY-12-0093.

(d) SRM-SECY-12-0093 is not a basis for shutting down or preventing the restart of an existing
plant.

SRM-SECY-12-0093 supports reasonable plant specific implementation schedules for GL 2004-
02. It does not require the imposition of any TSs or license conditions to shutdown or prevent
the restart of an existing plant, and none have been imposed for any plant. Therefore, the
assertion that SECY-12-0093 or SRM-SECY-12-0093 prevents the restart of Palisades is
without basis.

Based on the foregoing, the acceptance criteria in MD 8.11, DH Section III.C.1(a). are not met
since the facts specified in the petition do not constitute a basis for the requested action. Based
on this acceptance criteria not being met, our initial assessment is to not accept this submission
for review.
